<reason>A wins a competitive debate. B exposed a genuine difficulty in judging mixed well-being outcomes, but never established that a primary headline target must be one number. A directly answered the measurement and political-control questions with preannounced targets, independent methods, and continued reporting, while retaining GDP for fiscal and recession monitoring. Crucially, B’s insistence that GDP merely reports output left A’s harmful-growth counterexample substantially unanswered. A better justified changing the hierarchy of accountability; B more successfully defended GDP’s usefulness than its primacy.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s second pressure question asked how GDP avoids becoming an alibi when output rises while health and security worsen. B answered that GDP never claimed to measure health. A’s closing turned that narrowness against GDP’s entitlement to headline policy success—the clearest unresolved pressure in the exchange.</best_rebuttal>
